verdict: source retained with dependent obstruction demonstrated and graded claim separately verified
base_example: K=A=Z with identity augmentation, B=Z[X,Y2,Y3,...], Yj=gamma^jX, k=1. The printed4.12 right side S=ZX+B(X^2,Y2) is annihilated by e:B→Z[T],Y3↦T,all other positive generators↦0; Y3 in Fil^1B maps to T.

dependent_statements.claim: The4.12 decomposition is a direct sum of A-modules.
dependent_statements.assessment: The direct-sum presentation does not cover all Fil^1B: its addition map has image S and cannot hit Y3. The terms of S lie in disjoint weight ranges, but that injectivity does not supply the missing surjectivity.

dependent_statements.claim: The displayed coefficients belong to Fil^{k-j}A.
dependent_statements.assessment: For the unique monomial expansion this coefficient assertion follows from the explicit two-inclusion calculation in identification_337.json. It is not refuted by the failure of the preceding existence assertion.

dependent_statements.claim: 4.12 holds for every quotient by an augmentation-contained lambda-ideal.
dependent_statements.assessment: Take J=0, which is such a lambda-ideal, with q:B→B/J=B equal to the identity. The same e and Y3 give the same failure.

dependent_statements.claim: The analogous4.12 statement holds for a family of indeterminates.
dependent_statements.assessment: Take the singleton family {X1}. The lambda-isomorphism sending X1 to X and gamma^jX1 to Yj identifies its asserted formula with the failed example exactly.

dependent_statements.claim: An inverse is defined by the4.12 decomposition and4.13(i).
dependent_statements.assessment: That cited decomposition is unavailable on the representative Y3. Its class in Gr^1B is nevertheless zero, since Y3 is in Fil^3B. Thus this is a defect in the cited construction, not a counterexample to the graded formula. The coefficient construction in identification_337.json explicitly supplies mutually inverse maps for that formula.

related_336_ideal_assertion.source: The two paragraphs following4.12 call its right side an ideal and the family a ring filtration.
related_336_ideal_assertion.test: For k=1, X is in S but XY3 is not. Use the ordinary ring map h:B→Z[u,v]/(u^2) sending X to u,Y3 to v and all other positive generators to0. Then h(S)=Z u, while h(XY3)=uv is not in Z u; the polynomial basis modulo u^2 has independent u and uv terms.
related_336_ideal_assertion.conclusion: The stated right side is not even an ideal in this example. This explains why the following reduction cannot prove the displayed tail formula.

editorial_action: Retain all source body statements in both forms; attach this scope-specific note and the independent exact graded-map proof. No replacement theorem is proposed.
